name: Lightened Up Zucchini Gratin

ingredients.name: unsalted butter, room temperature, plus 1 1/2 tablespoons
dry white wine, such as Sauvignon Blanc

instructions.primary_message: Adjust oven rack to center position and preheat the oven to 205°C (400°F). In a medium skillet, melt 1 tablespoon butter over medium-low heat. Add the shallot, season with salt and pepper, and cook, stirring frequently, until softened, about 2 minutes. Add the garlic, and cook until fragrant, about 1 minute longer. Add the wine, bring the mixture up to a boil, then add the crème fraîche. Stir until melted, then remove from heat.

In a large bowl, add the zucchini, thyme, mint, and parsley. Season with salt and pepper, and add the shallot and wine mixture. Toss well and place in a lightly greased 9- by 33-cm rectangular baking dish. In another bowl, combine the crumbs, walnuts, cheese, and remaining 1 1/2 tablespoons butter with fingertips until the mixture is crumbly. Season with salt and pepper, and spread evenly over the zucchini. Drizzle lightly with olive oil (if using) and cover the baking dish with foil. Place the baking dish on a baking sheet, transfer to oven, then lower oven to 190°C (375°F).

Bake, covered, for 1 hour and 15 minutes. Remove foil, and bake uncovered until the topping is golden brown and crisp, 5 to 10 minutes. Transfer to a cooling rack and let cool 5 minutes before serving.

schema_metadata.keywords: creme fraiche, French in a Flash, gratins, zucchini

description: Gratin lightens up a little in this springtime take on a French home cooking classic. Zucchini is baked in a lightly creamy sauce of white wine and crème fraîche with mint, thyme, and parsley, all topped with crisp crust of breadcrumbs, Gruyère, Parmesan, and walnuts.
notes: Optional or for serving: Drizzle of extra virgin olive oil (optional)
author: Kerry Saretsky
